title: MVC
body:
A structural pattern splitting an application into three responsibilities. The **Model** owns data and business rules — validation, relationships, queries. The **View** owns presentation, turning data into HTML or [[JSON]]. The **Controller** is the coordinator: it receives the request, asks the model for what it needs, and picks a view to render.

The point is that each piece can change without dragging the others with it — a new output format is a view change, a new business rule is a model change. [[Ruby on Rails]] is the canonical implementation, with routes sitting in front to map URL + method onto a controller action. The same split shows up loosely in [[Express]] apps, where route handlers play the controller role.
